claims.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
claims.evidence: Let L be the initial number of live feature occurrences. Every legal no-teleport transition has distinct endpoints sharing a live feature and deletes that feature at both endpoints, so it removes at least two occurrences and never creates any. Hence a play has at most floor(L/2) transitions. A certificate is therefore a sequence of at most floor(L/2)+1 tile indices. A polynomial verifier checks distinct consecutive indices, computes the nonempty common live-feature set, deletes every common live feature at both endpoints, and accepts exactly when no occurrence remains. The L=0 case is handled directly. This is a complete NP-membership proof.
claims.witness: A certificate has the form (v_0,...,v_k), where k <= floor(L/2), and records the starting tile and every subsequent tile.
claims.search_method: Proved the monotone occurrence-count invariant and certificate-verification bound; additionally tested certificate verification and the two-occurrence decrease invariant during exhaustive finite searches.

claims.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
claims.evidence: Necessity: for a completed play, the transitions deleting feature f pair all vertices of its support S_f, producing a perfect matching M_f. An unordered tile pair cannot recur, because its first traversal deletes every then-live common feature and deleted occurrences never return. Thus the move sequence is an Euler trail of the simple union H of the M_f. If e=uv lies in H\M_f with u,v in S_f, then at least one f-occurrence was deleted before e, so m_f(u) or m_f(v) precedes e. Sufficiency: execute the stipulated Euler order and suppose the earliest matching event m_f(u) that fails finds f absent at u. An earlier nonmatching edge uw must have deleted it. Since m_f(u) is later, precedence for uw forces m_f(w) before uw. By earliestness, m_f(w) succeeded, so f was already absent at w when uw occurred; consequently uw could not have deleted f at u, a contradiction. Hence every matching event succeeds. Every H-edge belongs to some matching and is therefore legal when executed, and all occurrences are eventually deleted. Empty supports and the featureless instance give the empty matching/trail cases.
claims.witness: From a solution, take M_f to be the set of transitions that delete f. Conversely, the matching family and precedence-respecting Euler order themselves construct the solution.
claims.search_method: Completed independent necessity and earliest-failure sufficiency proofs. Compared direct dynamics, the characterization, and occurrence-mask reachability on all 139 distinct even-support families through four tiles, all 2,218 support-multiplicity-0/1/2 families through four tiles, and 1,344 bounded support multisets on five and six tiles; no discrepancy occurred.

claims.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
claims.evidence: A feature supported on exactly {u,v} can be deleted only by transition uv. All features with the same endpoint pair remain synchronized and one uv transition deletes all of them, so deduplicating endpoint pairs gives a simple graph K. Every solution must traverse every edge of K exactly once, while any Euler trail of K is legal because an untraversed pair-feature cannot have been deleted elsewhere. Thus solvability is equivalent to K being empty or having connected edge-bearing vertices and zero or two odd-degree vertices. Endpoint pairs can be formed, radix/counting-sorted, deduplicated, and subjected to connectivity and parity tests in linear time on the stated word-RAM representation. Arbitrarily many features may share one pair, so the sharing number is unbounded.
claims.witness: The decision instance reduces to the simple graph K containing one edge uv for every distinct two-tile feature support {u,v}; an Euler trail of K is exactly a no-teleport solution.
claims.search_method: Proved the forced-edge equivalence and exhaustively compared direct play, occurrence-mask search, and the Euler criterion on all 1,099 simple graphs through five vertices and all 5,325 choices formed by duplicating one present endpoint-pair feature.

claims.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
claims.evidence: For supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}, choose matchings 01, 02, 12, 03+12, and 04+12. Their simple union is the triangle 012 with leaves 03 and 04, hence it has an Euler trail from 3 to 4. In any actual solution the forced triangle is present, and tiles 3 and 4, each carrying only its respective four-support feature, must be the trail endpoints. Euler parity forces both leaves to attach to the same core vertex i. Starting from one leaf, the first triangle edge from i deletes at i the other leaf's feature, making the final move from i to that other leaf illegal; reversal is symmetric. Exhaustive search confirmed all 95 reachable states are nonsolving. Moreover, even if 'Eulerian' is interpreted strictly as admitting a circuit, two distinct features both supported on {0,1,2,3} are unsolvable, while choosing matchings 01+23 and 02+13 produces a connected 4-cycle with every degree two.
claims.witness: Primary witness: five tiles with feature supports [{0,1},{0,2},{1,2},{0,1,2,3},{0,1,2,4}] and displayed simple union {01,02,12,03,04}. Strict-circuit witness: two synchronized features both supported on {0,1,2,3}, with static matchings 01+23 and 02+13.
claims.search_method: Enumerated the complete dynamic state graph, every Euler-trail order of the displayed static union, and the precedence test using integer bit masks. Also checked the four-tile strict Euler-circuit witness exactly.

claims.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
claims.evidence: The current tile and L-bit live-occurrence mask determine every future move, giving at most n·2^L states. For each state, trying at most n-1 destinations and scanning the L incidences computes exactly the common live features and the resulting mask in O(nL) time. Every legal transition clears at least two bits, so the recurrence is acyclic and accepts exactly when it reaches mask zero. All starting tiles can use the same memo table. Hence time is O(n^2 L·2^L) and memo space is O(n·2^L), with the featureless case handled separately and input/recursion storage dominated for L>=1.
claims.witness: The recurrence is R(v,M)=true iff M=0 or some u!=v has a nonempty common-live-feature set and R(u,M')=true after clearing all corresponding endpoint occurrences.
claims.search_method: Implemented the claimed occurrence-mask recurrence independently and compared it with direct support-mask play search throughout the exhaustive characterization and frequency-two suites; every result agreed, and every visited-state count stayed below n·2^L.

target_evidence: The exact target demands a complete complexity classification for arbitrary sharing number, specifically a general polynomial-time algorithm or a matching hardness result. The draft provides neither: NP membership, an exact structural reformulation, a linear algorithm for a proper restricted class, a counterexample to a relaxation, and an exponential exact algorithm do not settle the general problem. All five are correct and material progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS applies. The draft explicitly labels its resolution PARTIAL and states that the general polynomial-versus-hardness question remains unresolved; that claimed resolution is ACCURATE rather than overstated or understated.
